      resp = future_tornado
    ),
  wave_3 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      resp = future_tornado
    ),

    transmute(

  wave_8 |>
    transmute(
      p_id,
      STUDY_AREA = study_area,
      resp = future_tornado
    )
) |>
  filter(!is.na(resp), !is.na(STUDY_AREA)) |>
  # A group with fewer than 20 respondents on this question is not charted.
  filter(n() >= 20, .by = STUDY_AREA)

# The survey is a panel, so one person can answer in several waves. The
# design clusters on the panelist: percentages are unweighted shares of
# responses, and the intervals allow for repeated answers.
est <- d |>
  as_survey_design(ids = p_id) |>
  group_by(STUDY_AREA, resp) |>
  summarise(
    p = survey_prop(proportion = TRUE, vartype = "ci"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

est <- est |>
  mutate(
    p = 100 * p, p_low = 100 * p_low, p_upp = 100 * p_upp,
    resp = factor(
      resp,
      levels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
      labels = c("Significantly decrease", "Decrease", "Stay about the same",
                 "Increase", "Significantly increase")
    ),
    STUDY_AREA = factor(
      STUDY_AREA,
      levels = c("Inside Little River Watershed",
                 "Outside Little River Watershed")
    )
  )

ggplot(est, aes(x = p, y = fct_rev(resp), fill = STUDY_AREA)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = p_low, xmax = p_upp),
    position = position_dodge2(reverse = TRUE),
    width = 0.2, linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  labs(
    title = str_wrap(paste(
      "When you think about the next 25 years in Oklahoma, do you",
      "think the risk (frequency and severity) of these weather",
      "hazards will increase, decrease, or stay about the same?",
      "Tornadoes"
    ), 70),
    x = "Share of respondents (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = "Little River watershed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
